objectives: Survey the 3D-printing + robotic-fabrication frontier — ICON, Tecla, Apis Cor, Mighty Buildings, ETH Gramazio Kohler, SAM.
Track the mass-timber tall-building revolution — Brock Commons, Mjøstårnet, Ascent Milwaukee, KPMB.
Explore smart cities + kinetic facades + AI in practice — Sidewalk Labs, Calatrava, Lynn animate form, LookX + Diagram + Spacemaker + the future role of the architect.

slides.title: 3D printing + robotic fabrication: ICON, Tecla, Apis Cor, ETH Gramazio Kohler
slides.body:
**Additive + robotic construction** is moving from research curiosity to commercial reality. Three threads matter: **concrete 3D printing** at building scale, **earthen + bio-based 3D printing**, and **robotic prefab + on-site fabrication**.

**Concrete 3D printing**:
- **ICON** (Austin TX, founded 2017 by Jason Ballard + Alex Le Roux): pioneered commercial 3D-printed homes. **Vulcan printer** — gantry-style extrusion, prints wall structure at ~13 mm/sec at scale. Lavacrete proprietary mix.
- ICON's projects: Wolf Ranch (Georgetown TX, 2022-) — first 100-home community of 3D-printed houses (with Lennar + BIG); Mars Dune Alpha (NASA habitat analog for crew isolation studies); Camp Mabry Marines barracks; Project Olympus (lunar construction R&D with NASA).
- **Apis Cor** (Russia/USA, founded 2014): mobile circular printer; printed a 38 m² house in Stupino Russia 24 hours (2017). Commercial buildings in Dubai + USA.
- **COBOD** (Denmark, BOD2 printer): gantry concrete printers used by many global partners.
- **CyBe Construction** (Netherlands): 6-axis robotic-arm concrete printers; commercial projects in Saudi Arabia, Oman.
- **Mighty Buildings** (Oakland CA, founded 2017): not concrete but UV-cured photopolymer composite + thermoset prints for ADUs + housing. Factory-scale prefab.
- **3D-printed walls + houses now in real markets**: ~$100-300/ft² range; structural code-approval increasing (ICC-ES, ETA-Denmark, UAE Dubai municipality). The cost + speed advantages will compound as material formulations + structural code recognition mature.

**Earthen + bio-based 3D printing**:
- **Tecla** (Bologna Italy 2021): Mario Cucinella Architects (MCA) + WASP (World's Advanced Saving Project) — 3D-printed earthen domed house using **on-site soil** + minimal additives. Two-armed Crane WASP printer. 60 m² 4.2 m high; 200 hours print + ~6 tonnes material from the site. Demonstrates an *almost-zero-carbon* + *almost-zero-transport* construction paradigm for emerging-market + low-resource contexts.
- **Mario Cucinella** (Italian architect, Bologna; founded MCA 1992; SOS School of Sustainability): leading sustainable + bio-climatic practice. CSET Center Ningbo; Nido d'Infanzia Guastalla; Cucinella's Italian Pavilion Expo Dubai 2020.
- **Hempcrete + bio-printing** (research): University of Maine BioHome3D printed entire small house (2022) with bio-based cellulose composite — recyclable, sequesters carbon. Branch Technology (Chattanooga TN): freeform polymer-fiber print bases for finish materials.

**Robotic fabrication — ETH Zurich + Gramazio Kohler Research**:
- **Fabio Gramazio + Matthias Kohler** — co-founded **Gramazio Kohler Research** at ETH Zurich (2005-). The leading academic laboratory for robotic construction worldwide.
- **Major projects**: Gantenbein vineyard facade (2006, the first robotically-bricklaid building); ETH NCCR Digital Fabrication research hub (2014-); the **DFAB House** at NEST Empa (2018) — first occupied building substantially constructed by robots: in-situ fabricator robot built mesh-mould reinforcement, smart slab printed, prefab timber assembled robotically.
- Gramazio Kohler's work demonstrates that robotic fabrication enables *non-standard repetition* — each brick or panel can be unique without economic penalty. Mass-customization of construction at unit cost.
- **Building research**: Block Research Group (Philippe Block, ETH) — geometric form-finding + unreinforced masonry shells with robotic prefab; NEST Hi-Lo unit, Armadillo Vault Venice Biennale 2016, the Striatus 3D-printed bridge Venice 2021.

**Other robotic-fabrication leaders**:
- **SAM (Semi-Automated Mason)** — Construction Robotics (NY); collaborative bricklaying robot. Field-deployed on commercial projects; lays ~3000 bricks per shift (vs ~500 for a human mason), with a human still placing the bricks the robot loads.
- **Hadrian X** (FBR Australia): autonomous brick-laying truck; lays full house in a few days. Commercial pilots in 2023+.
- **Built Robotics** (San Francisco, founded 2016 by Noah Ready-Campbell): autonomous earth-moving + grading equipment (excavators, dozers, skid steers). Site-prep automation.
- **Dusty Robotics** (founded 2018): FieldPrinter — autonomous floor-marking robot; prints construction layout lines from BIM model onto the slab. Standard on many commercial projects.
- **Boston Dynamics Spot** + **Spot Arm**: site monitoring + reality capture + selective tasks; widely piloted by construction firms (Skanska, Sundt, Bouygues, Foster + Partners).

**Why it matters**:
- **Productivity**: construction productivity has stagnated for decades while manufacturing + agriculture have grown (McKinsey, BCG analyses). Robotics + automation promise the long-awaited productivity step-change.
- **Quality + precision**: robotic + 3D-printed components within tolerance < ±1 mm vs ±5-10 mm for hand fabrication.
- **Labor**: aging skilled-trades workforce in many developed countries (US carpenter median age >43; bricklayers >45); automation augments + extends rather than displaces.
- **Carbon + waste**: factory + on-site additive processes reduce material waste vs subtractive + cut-fit construction.
- **New form-language**: non-standard geometries economically practical for the first time. The architectural vocabulary of *digital fabrication* (Gramazio Kohler, Block Research, MIT MAS, ICD Stuttgart) is reshaping what buildings look like.

slides.title: Mass timber + tall wood: Brock Commons, Mjøstårnet, Ascent Milwaukee, KPMB
slides.body:
**Mass timber tall buildings** — buildings of 8 stories and taller built with engineered timber (CLT, glulam, NLT, LVL, PSL) as the primary structure — have moved from research demonstration to commercial mainstream in less than a decade. Three drivers: **embodied-carbon imperative** (lesson 6), **code recognition** (IBC 2021 Type IV-A/B/C), and **CLT supply maturity** (Stora Enso + KLH + Binderholz + a growing North American supply chain).

**Key reference buildings**:

- **Stadthaus Murray Grove** (London, Waugh Thistleton Architects 2009): 9 stories, CLT panels + concrete plinth. The breakthrough demonstrating CLT structural feasibility for mid-rise; sparked the global CLT-in-tall-buildings movement.
- **Bridport House** (London, Karakusevic Carson 2011): 8 stories CLT residential.
- **Forté** (Melbourne, Lendlease 2012): 10 stories CLT; tallest mass-timber building globally at completion; demonstrated CLT in seismic Australia.
- **Treet** (Bergen Norway, Artec 2015): 14 stories, glulam mega-frame + CLT cores.
- **Brock Commons Tallwood House** (UBC Vancouver, Acton Ostry Architects + Fast + Epp engineers 2017): **18 stories, 53 m** — held the *tallest mass-timber building* title 2017-2019. Hybrid: concrete cores + foundation + 1st floor; CLT floors + glulam columns above. Demonstrated rapid construction (~9 weeks of mass-timber erection for 17 floors).
- **Mjøstårnet** (Brumunddal Norway, Voll Arkitekter + Sweco engineers 2019): **18 stories, 85.4 m** — the tallest pure mass-timber building globally at completion (no concrete superstructure). Glulam mega-columns + glulam mega-trusses + CLT floors. Hotel + apartments + offices + restaurants + swimming pool.
- **Sara Cultural Centre** (Skellefteå Sweden, White Arkitekter 2021): **20 stories, 75 m** — tallest mass-timber building at completion. Library + theatres + hotel + restaurants. Mjøs equivalent in Sweden.
- **Ascent Milwaukee** (Korb + Associates + Thornton Tomasetti 2022): **25 stories, 86.6 m** — current world's tallest mass-timber building. Hybrid: concrete cores; CLT floors + glulam columns on floors 7-25. Residential.
- **Hoho Vienna** (Rüdiger Lainer + Partner 2019): 24 stories hybrid.
- **Limberlost Place** (Toronto, **Acton Ostry + KPMB** + Moriyama Teshima 2024): 10 stories mass timber; George Brown College net-zero academic building.
- **KPMB (Kuwabara Payne McKenna Blumberg, Toronto)**: leading firm in Canadian mass-timber + sustainable institutional design; Limberlost Place; Brock University. KPMB's institutional + academic mass-timber work has been influential globally.
- **80 M Street SE** (Washington DC, Hickok Cole 2022): mass-timber **office** addition retrofit onto an existing concrete building — first major US commercial mass-timber addition.
- **Schaffer Project / T3 Bayside** (Toronto, 3XN/3XN + Adjaye): proposed 35-story timber.

**Code recognition**:
- **IBC 2021 (International Building Code)** added **Type IV-A, IV-B, IV-C** mass-timber construction types: up to **18 stories** for Type IV-A (with full encapsulation), permitting tall mass-timber buildings under building code rather than requiring case-by-case Alternative Materials, Design and Methods Request (AMMR).
- **NBCC 2020** (Canada) parallel updates.
- **Eurocode 5** + national annexes (Germany, Austria, Sweden, Finland, Norway, UK): mature CLT structural design; ETA-Denmark + ETA-Europe certifications.
- **Fire performance**: mass timber chars at ~38 mm/hr but retains structural strength inside the char; predictable + code-recognized 1-2 hour ratings. Multiple full-scale fire tests by USDA FPL, NRC Canada, ASTM E119 + ISO 834 protocols.

**Supply chain (recapping lesson 3)**:
- **Stora Enso** (Finland/Sweden, largest CLT producer globally): Ybbs + Bad St. Leonhard mills + multiple national + import operations.
- **KLH** (Austria, the CLT originator).
- **Binderholz** (Austria/Germany/UK/US): integrated forestry + CLT + glulam.
- **MyTi** (Canada): Quebec-based CLT producer.
- **Vaagen Timbers, SmartLam, DRJ** (US): expanding domestic North American supply.
- **Katerra** (US, founded 2015, defunct 2021): vertically integrated mass-timber + prefab; cautionary tale of scaling-too-fast.
- **Mercer International, Sterling Solutions**: integrated forest + mill operations.

**Embodied-carbon dividend (recapping lesson 6)**:
- A typical mass-timber building has ~50% lower cradle-to-gate embodied carbon than equivalent concrete or steel.
- Sustainably-harvested wood **sequesters CO₂** in the structure (~1 t CO₂ per m³ of dry timber); cradle-to-gate net carbon can be *negative* when biogenic carbon is credited (per EN 16485).
- Switching the structural system from concrete or steel to mass timber is **the highest-leverage embodied-carbon move** available in current practice (AIA 2030, RIBA 2030, Architecture 2030 modeling).

**Construction advantages**:
- **Prefab + precision**: CNC-cut CLT + glulam panels + connectors. ±1 mm tolerances.
- **Speed**: panels arrive sized + numbered; assembled with cranes + standard hand-tools; floors erected in days per level (Brock Commons: 17 floors in ~9 weeks).
- **Cleaner sites**: less dust + noise + waste; fewer trades on-site.
- **Lighter weight**: ~1/5 the weight of equivalent concrete → lighter foundations + better seismic performance.

**Open challenges**:
- **Acoustic** detailing for residential (floor-ceiling assemblies need careful design; CLT + concrete topping is common).
- **Long-span limitation** — CLT plate spans typically ≤ 7 m without composite + post-tensioning.
- **Cost premium** in some markets (until supply chain matures locally).
- **Forest stewardship + supply** (FSC + PEFC certification, regional CLT mills + sourcing).

Mass timber is the most important structural-material development since reinforced concrete + steel; lesson 3 covered the material itself, and this lesson documents the buildings that have brought it to scale.

slides.title: Smart cities + kinetic + AI in practice: Sidewalk Labs, Calatrava, Lynn, the architect's future
slides.body:
The contemporary frontier of architecture also encompasses **smart-city + responsive buildings**, **AI-augmented design + practice**, and the **evolving role of the architect** itself. The discipline's last decade and next decade can be read through these threads.

**Smart cities + sensor-instrumented buildings**:
- **Sidewalk Labs** (Google/Alphabet 2015-): proposed smart-city development at Quayside Toronto (Sidewalk Toronto, 2017-2020); abandoned May 2020 amid privacy + governance controversy + COVID disruption. The project's ambition (sensor-instrumented neighborhood, modular construction, data-driven adaptive infrastructure) + its failure are both instructive. Hypar (Anthony Hauck, lesson 7) emerged in part from Sidewalk Labs's generative-design experiments.
- **Songdo** (South Korea, KPF master plan 2003-): purpose-built smart city — embedded sensors, pneumatic-tube waste collection, deep building-management integration. Mixed reception.
- **Masdar City** (Abu Dhabi, Foster + Partners 2007-): planned zero-carbon eco-city; partially built; scaled back.
- **Toyota Woven City** (Mount Fuji Japan, BIG master plan 2020-): prototype city for autonomous mobility + smart-home tech; under construction 2024-.
- **The Line / NEOM** (Saudi Arabia, Morphosis + Mark Foster Gage 2021-): 170 km linear city megaproject; controversial; under planning + construction.
- **Lessons**: top-down smart-city projects often fail or pivot; bottom-up sensor + data integration in conventional cities + buildings (Local Law 97 NYC, building benchmarking ordinances, IoT-instrumented retrofit) yields more practical impact.

**Kinetic + responsive facades + architecture**:
- **Santiago Calatrava** (Spanish-Swiss engineer + architect, 1951-): kinetic + biomorphic structural expressions. **Milwaukee Art Museum Quadracci Pavilion** (2001): the **Burke Brise Soleil** — moveable sun-screen wings with 72-tonne spans, opening + closing twice daily — became the iconic kinetic-architecture image. World Trade Center Transportation Hub Oculus (NYC, 2016) is also responsive (opens for ventilation + ceremony). Other Calatrava: Turning Torso Malmö (2005), Athens Olympics 2004 venues, Valencia City of Arts + Sciences.
- **Al Bahar Towers** (Abu Dhabi, AHR 2012): mashrabiya-inspired responsive sun-screen facade; ~1000 kinetic origami elements opening + closing with sun position.
- **Greg Lynn — animate form**: American architect + theorist; *Animate Form* (1999) — early advocacy of dynamic + responsive form generated through animation software (Maya, Houdini). Lynn argued architecture should be conceived as participating in environmental + temporal flow rather than as static object. Influenced parametric + computational generation (lesson 7). His Embryological House (1997-) + Korean Presbyterian Church Queens (1999) are early manifestations.
- **Adaptive + smart facades**: integrated PV (BIPV), electrochromic glazing (View Inc., SageGlass — voltage-controlled tint), thermo-bimetal shading (Doris Sung), shape-memory polymer + alloy facades. Allianz Arena LED facade (Munich 2005, Herzog & de Meuron) — color-changing skin.
- **Embedded sensors + actuators**: occupancy + CO₂ + humidity + air-quality + light + thermal sensors driving real-time HVAC + shading + lighting control. The Edge (Amsterdam, PLP 2014, Deloitte): ~30000 sensors; widely cited as the smartest office building.

**Generative + AI in practice (recapping + extending lesson 7)**:
- **LookX, Diagram, Spacemaker (now Autodesk Forma), Hypar, Maket, Veras, PromeAI**: rapidly evolving AI tools for concept generation, plan generation, rendering, code-checking, programming.
- **LLM-augmented Revit + Dynamo**: natural-language model queries + scripts; Microsoft + Autodesk + GitHub Copilot integrations.
- **Hassell + AI experiments (2022-)**: Hassell published *AI Designed Hospital* + other speculations; one of the most aggressive AI-first practices.
- **Foster + Partners ARD, SOM, ZHA, BIG, KPF, Gensler, KPMB**: each have applied-research groups developing AI + generative tooling.
- **2024 frontier projects**: AI plan-generation tools producing buildable-quality residential + multifamily plans from natural-language briefs (early-stage; quality + code-compliance varies); generative facade systems; LLM-driven code-compliance checking (Hypar, Microsoft).

**Architect's role: future trajectories**:
- **Curator + integrator**: as AI handles ideation + drafting + analysis, the architect's distinct value is design judgment, integration across systems, ethics + responsibility, client + user empathy, regulatory + code expertise, stewardship of place + culture.
- **Generalist + specialist coexist**: specialist roles in design technology, building science, sustainability, computational design grow; generalist principal-in-charge roles remain.
- **License + liability**: the AIA + state architectural licensing boards + RIBA + national equivalents continue to require human architects of record. AI augments + accelerates; doesn't replace responsibility.
- **Climate adaptation specialist**: as climate impacts intensify, architecture's adaptation role (flood resilience, heat mitigation, fire-resistant detailing in WUI zones, water-scarcity-aware design, retrofit + adaptive reuse) becomes central.
- **Post-pandemic spaces**: COVID-19 reshaped workplace + healthcare + residential design — flexibility, IAQ + ventilation (lesson 5), hybrid-work-aware programming, multifamily housing reshaped for at-home work. WELL + Fitwel emphasis on air + occupant health surged.
- **Equity + justice**: environmental justice (Klinenberg + lesson 6), inclusive design, affordable housing crisis (US + UK + EU), informal-settlement upgrading (Aravena Quinta Monroy 2003, Pritzker 2016), the *right to the city* (Lefebvre + Harvey). Equity is now an explicit category in many certifications (LBC Equity petal).

**AI ethics in architecture**:
- **Training-data bias**: models trained on existing architectural imagery encode the discipline's historical biases — Western + male + monumental + camera-friendly buildings overrepresented.
- **Authorship + IP**: who owns AI-generated design? Whose work was in the training set? Open + unresolved.
- **Labor + displacement**: AI may displace junior staff who learn through drafting + technical drawings; mentorship + training pathways need to adapt.
- **Climate impact of training compute**: large models consume significant energy + water; ironic for a discipline focused on sustainability.
- **Access + equity**: AI tools are mostly subscription-based; gap between large-firm + small-firm + global-North + global-South capability widens.

**The discipline's next decade** is being shaped simultaneously by:
- Climate adaptation + decarbonization (lessons 3, 6).
- The mass-timber revolution (this lesson + lesson 3).
- 3D printing + robotic fabrication (this lesson).
- AI-augmented design + practice (lessons 7 + this).
- Equity + justice + post-pandemic programmatic shifts.
- The endurance of place + culture + craft + the Vitruvian triad (lesson 1).

Architecture has always been a discipline of synthesis — structural, programmatic, material, aesthetic, ethical. The contemporary frontier expands that synthesis to include the algorithmic, the climatic, and the just. The architect's task — orchestrating all of this into buildings that stand, serve, and please — remains, in essence, Vitruvian. The tools + materials + responsibilities have multiplied; the discipline persists.

question.question: Evaluate mass timber for an 18-story affordable-housing project
question.goal: A developer wants to build an 18-story 200-unit affordable-housing tower in a mid-size US city. Walk through whether mass timber (CLT + glulam) is feasible + advantageous compared to conventional reinforced concrete.

steps.prompt: Is 18 stories feasible in mass timber under the current US building code, and what reference projects support the decision?

acceptedAnswers: yes — IBC 2021 Type IV-A allows up to 18 stories with full encapsulation, and precedent buildings include Brock Commons UBC 18 stories, Mjøstårnet Norway 18 stories, Ascent Milwaukee 25 stories, Sara Cultural Centre Skellefteå 20 stories

steps.reveal: **IBC 2021 Type IV-A** permits mass-timber buildings up to **18 stories** with full encapsulation (gypsum protection to all timber surfaces, increased fire ratings). Reference projects: **Brock Commons UBC 2017** (18 stories, hybrid), **Mjøstårnet 2019** (18 stories, pure mass timber), **Sara Cultural Centre Skellefteå 2021** (20 stories), **Ascent Milwaukee 2022** (25 stories — current world's tallest mass-timber). 18 stories is now mainstream + code-supported. Pre-2021 these would have required AMMR (Alternative Materials, Design and Methods Request) approvals.

steps.prompt: What is the embodied-carbon advantage vs reinforced concrete equivalent?

acceptedAnswers: mass timber typically 40 to 50 percent lower cradle-to-gate embodied carbon than reinforced concrete equivalent, and net carbon negative when biogenic sequestration is credited per EN 16485 — the single highest-leverage embodied-carbon move available

steps.reveal: **Mass timber** structure typically has **40-50% lower cradle-to-gate embodied carbon** than reinforced concrete equivalent (per Hammond + Jones ICE + EC3 data + Architecture 2030 modeling). With **biogenic carbon credited** (per EN 16485 + EU LULUCF accounting), the structural system can be **net carbon-negative** — storing more CO₂ in the structure than the cradle-to-gate process emits. **The single highest-leverage embodied-carbon move** available to architects + developers (lessons 3 + 6). For an 18-story 200-unit building this can translate to ~1500-3000 tonnes CO₂e saved + ~500-1500 tonnes sequestered.

steps.prompt: What construction-speed + cost advantages are typical, and what trade-offs?

acceptedAnswers: construction speed often 20 to 40 percent faster than RC due to CNC-cut prefab panels (Brock Commons completed 17 floors in 9 weeks), lighter weight reduces foundation cost, but in many markets material cost is currently 5 to 15 percent premium until local CLT supply matures

steps.reveal: **Speed**: 20-40% faster than RC; CNC-cut + numbered + crane-erected panels. Brock Commons UBC erected 17 floors of mass timber in **9 weeks**. **Weight**: ~1/5 of concrete equivalent → smaller foundations, better seismic performance. **Cleaner site**: less waste, dust, noise, fewer trades on-site. **Cost**: currently 5-15% material premium in many North American markets (Vaagen, SmartLam, MyTi expanding domestic capacity); Stora Enso + Binderholz + KLH supply much of the EU. Often offset by speed + financing savings. **Acoustic + fire detailing** + connection details add design effort upfront.

steps.prompt: Summarize the decision + name the structural + sustainability consultants that would be on the project.

acceptedAnswers: recommend mass timber for embodied-carbon + speed + tenant + ESG appeal; engage a mass-timber structural engineer (Fast + Epp, Equilibrium, StructureCraft, Thornton Tomasetti mass-timber group), an acoustic consultant, a fire engineer experienced in IBC Type IV-A, a CLT supplier (Stora Enso or Binderholz or MyTi or SmartLam), and a sustainability consultant for LCA + LEED + RIBA 2030 verification

steps.reveal: **Recommend mass timber** for the embodied-carbon dividend + speed + tenant + ESG + occupant-health appeal — addressing AIA 2030 + RIBA 2030 + likely future regulation. **Team**: **mass-timber structural engineer** (Fast + Epp who did Brock Commons, Equilibrium Consulting, StructureCraft, Thornton Tomasetti Mass Timber Group, Holmes Solutions); **acoustic consultant** (Cerami, Talaske, Threshold); **fire engineer** experienced in IBC Type IV-A (Arup Fire, Jensen Hughes); **CLT supplier** (Stora Enso, Binderholz, KLH, MyTi, SmartLam, Vaagen); **sustainability consultant** for LCA (EC3 + OneClickLCA), LEED/Passivhaus + RIBA 2030 verification. Lesson 5's coordination + lesson 7's BIM clash detection essential — mass timber's tight tolerances + acoustic + fire detailing require careful coordination.

question.question: Why is Ascent Milwaukee (2022, Korb + Associates + Thornton Tomasetti) considered a milestone in mass-timber construction?
options: It was the first wood-framed building.

Ascent Milwaukee (Korb + Associates Architects + Thornton Tomasetti structural engineers, 2022) is currently the **world's tallest mass-timber building** at **25 stories + 86.6 m** — surpassing Mjøstårnet Norway (18 stories, 85.4 m, 2019) by a single story + 1.2 m. Hybrid structural system: **concrete core + foundation + lower floors; CLT floors + glulam columns on floors 7-25**. **Residential program** — ~259 luxury apartments. Demonstrates: (1) mass timber's commercial viability at high-rise residential scale + above-18-stories territory (under IBC AMMR + Wisconsin code variance); (2) hybrid systems (concrete core for stiffness + glulam + CLT above) are practical + economical; (3) major US developer + general contractor + AHJ acceptance. **Embodied carbon** ~50% lower than equivalent RC. Combined with Sara Cultural Centre (2021, 20 stories), Mjøstårnet (2019, 18 stories), Brock Commons (2017, 18 stories), Stadthaus Murray Grove (2009, 9 stories), Ascent marks the mass-timber transition from research demonstration to mainstream commercial construction.
question.explanation: Ascent Milwaukee (Korb + Associates + Thornton Tomasetti, 2022) is currently the world's tallest mass-timber building at 25 stories / 86.6 m, surpassing Mjøstårnet (18 stories, 85.4 m, 2019). Hybrid: concrete core + foundation + lower floors, CLT floors + glulam columns floors 7-25. Residential. Demonstrates mass timber's commercial viability above 18 stories under IBC AMMR + state code variance + ~50% lower embodied carbon vs RC equivalent. With Sara Cultural Centre, Mjøstårnet, Brock Commons, Stadthaus Murray Grove, marks the transition from research to mainstream commercial.

question.question: Plot a 10-year practice roadmap
question.prompt: You are the founding partner of a 40-person architecture firm in 2024 contemplating where the discipline is moving. Plot a 10-year roadmap that addresses: (a) materials + decarbonization — mass timber, low-carbon concrete, embodied + operational carbon; (b) fabrication + delivery — 3D printing (ICON, Tecla, Apis Cor, Mighty Buildings), robotic prefab (ETH Gramazio Kohler, SAM, Hadrian X), digital twins for FM; (c) digital + AI tooling — BIM maturation, parametric, AI generative + LLM-augmented practice (Forma, Hypar, LookX, Diagram, Hassell-style experiments); (d) practice + role evolution — the architect as curator + integrator + climate-adaptation specialist + post-pandemic-spaces designer; (e) ethics + equity + AI bias + IP. Which two investments would you make first + why?

question.question: Brock Commons UBC erected its 17 mass-timber floors in approximately 9 weeks. Roughly, how many floors per week did its crew install (to one decimal place)?

question.prompt: In ≤150 words, explain how the architect's role is evolving under the combined pressure of climate + decarbonization + AI + new materials + post-pandemic programs — and which Vitruvian-era continuities persist.
question.rubric: Mentions: the contemporary architect's role is being reshaped by multiple simultaneous pressures: **decarbonization** (AIA 2030 + RIBA 2030 + Architecture 2030 + embodied + operational carbon, mass timber + lesson 6 certification stack), **new materials + fabrication** (CLT, ETFE, 3D printing — ICON Vulcan, Tecla Cucinella, Apis Cor, Mighty Buildings + robotic fab — ETH Gramazio Kohler, SAM, Hadrian X), **AI augmentation** (Forma née Spacemaker, Hypar, LookX, Diagram, Midjourney + Stable Diffusion concept imagery, LLM-augmented BIM, Hassell early experiments), **climate adaptation** (flood + heat + fire + WUI), **post-pandemic spaces** (flexibility, IAQ, WELL, hybrid-work programs), **equity + justice** (Aravena's incremental housing, LBC Equity petal). The architect's role becomes: **curator + integrator + climate-adaptation specialist** — selecting + refining AI-generated options, integrating across systems + materials + ethics, taking professional responsibility, stewarding place + culture. Continuities: the **Vitruvian triad** (firmitas + utilitas + venustas, lesson 1) persists — structure, function, beauty are still the discipline's irreducible commitments. Drawing, sketching, modeling, the studio, the parti, the reflective practice (Schön + lesson 4), precedent-based reasoning (Rossi + Alexander + Pallasmaa + Frampton) — all continue. Tools + materials + responsibilities have multiplied; the discipline persists.
